_readme: Reproducibility contract for Ruckel's self-built minimal static FFmpeg (ADR-0029).
Pins the FFmpeg/x264/dav1d sources by version + SHA-256 and the full configure flag
sets; the FFmpeg flags are the ADR-0028 decode matrix expressed mechanically.
scripts/build-ffmpeg/build.ps1 consumes this file and installs static libs + headers
+ .pc files into the gitignored src-tauri/ffmpeg-libs/, stamped with this file's
SHA-256. src-tauri/build.rs fails the cargo build loudly if the stamp does not match
(stale-build guard), so any edit to this file requires re-running the build script.
--prefix is machine-dependent and injected by the script; it is deliberately not
pinned here. This manifest doubles as the GPL-compliance record (ADR-0003):
FFmpeg and x264 are GPL, dav1d is BSD-2 (its license text ships in the repo-root

x264._note: GitHub mirror of code.videolan.org/videolan/x264 — the upstream GitLab gates its archive endpoint behind an Anubis proof-of-work challenge, so tarballs cannot be fetched from it mechanically. The commit hash pins the content; the SHA-256 additionally pins the GitHub-generated tarball bytes (if GitHub ever regenerates archives differently, the download step fails loudly and this pin gets refreshed).

ffmpeg._note: n7.1.x stable series — the same major version v1 shipped, within rsmpeg's supported range (ADR-0029).

nasm._note: Native win64 NASM pinned as a build tool (not linked into anything) so the assembler is not at the mercy of whatever is on PATH; used by all three builds.

configure._x264Note: bit-depth/chroma-format are pinned to the output contract (ADR-0006: H.264 high profile, yuv420p — 8-bit 4:2:0 only; the mandatory format=yuv420p filter stage guarantees the encoder never sees anything else). -MD matches the Rust msvc target's default dynamic CRT; one CRT family end to end.
configure._ffmpegNote: The enable-demuxer/decoder/parser/filter enumerations are the ADR-0028 matrix (with one issue-05 arbiter addition: the `flv` decoder, for the committed flv1+mp3/flv corpus cell — FLV1/Sorenson is decoded by `flv`, distinct from `h263`; the matrix-drift test caught it stranded). the filter list is ADR-0027's minimal libavfilter. --enable-avdevice deviates from the ADR-0027 letter ('avdevice compiled out'): rusty_ffmpeg's Windows link path unconditionally links all seven libav libs, so libavdevice is built as an empty stub — zero input/output devices are enabled (--disable-everything covers them), it merely satisfies the link list. bcrypt has no --enable flag and is not governed by --disable-autodetect either: configure's plain system check enables it on msvc unconditionally, so avutil's av_get_random_seed uses BCryptGenRandom and bcrypt.lib must be linked — exactly ADR-0029's 'bcrypt for RNG' expectation.

linking.rsmpegDiscovery: FFMPEG_LIBS_DIR + FFMPEG_INCLUDE_DIR env vars, set repo-relatively in the committed .cargo/config.toml [env] section. rusty_ffmpeg's build.rs has no pkg-config path on Windows (its windows branch only supports libs-dir or vcpkg), so the pkg-config-vs-env-vars question from ADR-0029 resolved itself: env vars. Binding generation runs bindgen at cargo build time and needs libclang (LIBCLANG_PATH).
linking.staticLibNaming: FFmpeg's msvc toolchain mode and meson emit a mix of <name>.lib / lib<name>.a; rusty_ffmpeg emits cargo:rustc-link-lib=static=<name>, which the MSVC linker resolves as <name>.lib — so build.ps1 normalizes every static lib in ffmpeg-libs/lib to <name>.lib. One exception: FFmpeg's configure hardcodes -lx264 -> libx264.lib for msvc (matching x264's own cl build output), so libx264.lib keeps its name and build.rs links static=libx264.
linking._note: rusty_ffmpeg links only the seven libav libs; x264, dav1d and the Windows system libs are emitted by src-tauri/build.rs. windowsSystemLibs was resolved empirically by the ADR-0027 tracer slice: bcrypt (avutil av_get_random_seed -> BCryptGenRandom) and nothing else. Note these directives ride on the ruckel lib target — binaries/tests must link ruckel_lib to inherit them.
